title: Split Array Largest Sum
statement: Split the list into exactly k non-empty contiguous pieces so that the largest piece sum is as small as possible. Return that smallest possible largest sum. (1 <= k <= len(nums), values are non-negative.)

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(20)
    return [[r.randint(0, 10000) for _ in range(5000)], 50]

hints.1_question: If someone proposes a maximum allowed piece sum, can you quickly tell how many pieces you would need? What happens to that count as the allowed sum grows?
hints.2_nudge: Binary search the answer. It can't be below the largest element and never needs to exceed the total sum. Greedily fill pieces up to the cap.
hints.3_big_hint: lo = max(nums), hi = sum(nums). parts(cap) counts greedy pieces. If parts(mid) <= k: hi = mid else lo = mid + 1.

known_bugs.name: lower bound of 1 allows pieces smaller than the biggest element
known_bugs.followup: Can any piece have a sum smaller than the biggest single element? What is the smallest sensible cap?

known_bugs.name: upper bound one too small
known_bugs.followup: With k = 1 the only piece is everything. Is that sum inside your search range?

known_bugs.name: piece counter starts at 0
known_bugs.followup: If everything fits in one piece, how many pieces does your counter report?

followups: Why is a greedy fill optimal for the feasibility check?
How would dynamic programming solve this, and why is binary search faster?
